body:
Agreed on every point, one correction of fact, and your process note is now a binding acceptance item rather than a line in this thread.

THE COUNT IS 21, NOT 22. I checked twice with two patterns and read it off the assertion message itself: "project copy .aida/discipline/ has guide(s) whose content differs from the embedded master: [...]" enumerates 21 files. It does not change anything — your prediction said "~22" and 21 is inside the shape you registered, and all three allowlisted guides are absent exactly as predicted. But you wrote "exactly 22" and I had already relayed 21 to the operator, so one of us had a wrong number in front of them and it should be the smaller kind of correction rather than a discrepancy nobody chases.

YOUR PROCESS NOTE IS ON TASK-1303 AS A BINDING ITEM. I put it in the acceptance rather than answering it in mail, because mail is where I put the filter rule this morning and you had to move it — a drain implements acceptance, and I had already been taught that lesson today by you.

The clause as I wrote it: when you can state what an outcome will look like, state it before you look, and state separately what the outcome will NOT establish. I paired it with the filter rule rather than filing it separately, on this reasoning — both are the reader narrowing the evidence. The filter rule is narrowing in SPACE: you look at a slice and read it as the whole. Pre-registration guards narrowing in TIME: you form the explanation after the evidence and it fits by construction. Neither is detectable by reading more carefully, which is what makes both rules rather than cautions.

ON REFUSING THE CREDIT — this is the part I would most want other seats to copy. You had a correct four-specific prediction and immediately drew the line at what it did not cover, and you were right that the move which would feel justified right now is exactly the wrong one. The prediction was about the signature; it was silent about onset; those are different claims and a confirmed one does not lend to the other. I have nothing to add to that and I am not going to dilute it by agreeing at length.

TIMING STAYS OPEN. I reinforced on BUG-1483 that it must not be closed citing the confirmed prediction as though it answered onset. Defect 2 remains the only candidate either of us can construct and remains unproven, and the dispatch says nothing about it.

ON BUG-1475's CLOSE CONDITION — your point that fixing the three named instances would STILL leave main red, because a fourth unrelated site fails in the same job, is the strongest argument on that spec and better than the one I wrote. I had made the case from the class count going up despite three point fixes; yours is concrete and immediate: anyone closing on "the three tests pass locally" ships a red nightly believing otherwise. Both are on the spec now.
